title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-taylor-nguyen
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for the regional failover + smart-routing fallback incident (2026-03-03 -> 03-04). Mostly breadcrumbs of commands, logs, quick hypotheses. This is informal - intended for the oncall who inherits and for triage followups.

Summary:
- At ~2026-03-03T14:08Z customers in eu-west started seeing elevated 5xx from Hosted API routes that should fallback to dedicated variants.
- Smart routing tried to reroute to eu-central as configured but many requests ended up 503/backpressure errors (no healthy upstream) or long tail latency that triggered circuit breakers.
- Automatic fallback to lower-tier region (us-west) occurred for some flows but created cross-region latencies and triggered rate-limit protection, causing additional failed requests.

What I observed (timeline):
- 14:05 UTC: first alerts - increased error rate for model route: open-llama-65b/zero-shot in eu-west.
- 14:06-14:12: repeated health checks show intermittent pod restarts on eu-west pool (OOM in worker-3), see kube logs below.
- 14:12: routing controller marked region unhealthy; policy should prefer regional fallback to eu-central then us-west.
- 14:13-14:25: large spike in routed traffic to eu-central; many requests hit kv-cache warmup and experienced 2-5s cold starts; latency caused queue growth and proxy 503s.
- 14:26: cascading circuit-breaker trips on eu-central -> fallback to us-west; some requests succeeded but SLO breach.

Commands I ran (most useful):
- kubectl -n serving logs worker-3 --since=30m -c runtime
  -> repeated java/lang/OutOfMemoryError stack trace + GC thrashing at 14:07-14:10

- kubectl -n routing get pods -o wide | grep eu-west
  -> multiple pods OnRestarting/CrashLoopBackOff around 14:08-14:11

- curl -sS -H 'x-api-key: <redacted>' 'https://routing.internal/v1/route?model=open-llama-65b&region=eu-west' | jq
  -> response: {"status":"degraded","fallback_candidate":"eu-central","reason":"no_healthy_upstream"} 

- ssh to eu-central proxy (10.2.6.45) and tail proxy logs:
  -> 14:14:22 proxy: upstream_timeout for session=...
  -> 14:16:01 proxy: queue_depth=512, max_conn=600, rejecting new conn -> 503

- redis-cli -h kv-cache-eu-west info
  -> keyspace hit-rate low (~12%) due to recent pool restarts; cache warmup ongoing

- checked circuit breaker metrics (PromQL):
  sum(rate(cb_tripped_total{region="eu-central",route="open-llama-65b"}[1m]))
  -> spike starting 14:15, consistent for ~6m

Relevant log/error snippets:
- runtime worker-3: "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space"
- proxy eu-central: "upstream_timeout: call took 5.03s, threshold=5.0s"
- routing-controller: "Marked region eu-west unhealthy (consecutive_failures=5, last_failure=2026-03-03T14:10:26Z)"
- rate-limiter: "client_rate_limit_exceeded: client=acct_24, policy=global_burst, limit=100rps"

Configuration/context to check:
- Smart routing policy (prod): priority: [regional, alternate_region, global_graceful_fallback]
  - fallback ordering: eu-west -> eu-central -> us-west
  - circuit breaker thresholds per region: latency 95th > 1.2s AND 5xx% > 1.5% for 2m -> trip
  - healthcheck: consecutive_failures=5, interval=10s

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: Root cause was resource exhaustion (OOM) on eu-west worker pool -> healthcheck flapping -> mass reroutes. Reroutes overwhelmed eu-central because its routing had insufficient headroom or aggressive circuit breakers/trip thresholds.
2) Secondary: Cache warmup (KV cache) on eu-central created transient cold latencies; combined with high burst traffic from reroutes produced queue buildup and triggered proxy 503s.
3) Tertiary: Fallback policy ordering + sudden client retry behaviour (clients retry on 5xx) amplified load across fallback regions. Retry budget not honored causing amplification.
4) Edge: Config drift - one of the eu-central nodes had an older kernel/driver, reducing perf under high load; need to confirm via image tags.

Quick mitigations attempted (and outcome):
- Scaled eu-central pool up by +30% (kubectl scale deployment routing-eu-central --replicas=26) at 14:20 -> helped capacity but took ~90s to warm up; partial easing of 503s after 14:23.
- Adjusted circuit-breaker thresholds to be slightly more permissive for 5m window (temporary) -> reduced trips but increased tail latency; reverted at 15:10.
- Increased KV cache prefetch concurrency on eu-central for model open-llama-65b -> improved hit-rate from 12% -> 58% by 14:40.
- Disabled client-level aggressive retries for a subset of noisy clients via a temporary config in rate-limiter -> decreased amplification.

Outstanding questions / things to validate:
- Which worker(s) in eu-west had OOM? Is the heap size configured correctly? Did a model update push a heavier memory config? (Check deployment image tag and JVM flags).
- Were there any infra maintenance events in eu-central (kernel updates, nvidia-driver restarts) around the same time? (Check infra change log and node-restart audit).
- Are client SDKs honoring Retry-After headers? Which callers kept retrying too aggressively? (analyze access logs for retry loops).
- Was the fallback ordering correct in the policy we read? Confirm git history of routing policy pushed 2026-02-25.

Next steps / TODOs (owners):
- [Ethan Park] Extract detailed pod OOM events and deployment image+JVM flags for eu-west workers. command: kubectl describe pod worker-3 -n serving | grep -A4 Events (due EOD today).
- [Olivia Chen] Correlate infra node events (reboots, driver updates) across eu-west/eu-central from 2026-03-03 13:30 -> 15:00. (Check cloud provider activity logs).
- [Samir Patel] Run heap dump analysis for affected runtime pod (if available) and confirm memory leak vs transient spike. location: /var/dumps on node.
- [Taylor Nguyen (me)] Audit routing policy commit history and verify fallback ordering; open PR to add conservative backoff on first fallback.
- [SRE rotation] Add temporary rule to reduce automatic cross-region fallbacks for 30m for noisy clients.

Longer term action items (for postmortem):
- Add pre-warming policy for KV cache on fallback regions when a region is marked unhealthy (warm caches proactively before shifting traffic).
- Rework circuit breaker trip rules to prefer fail-open for short bursts but degrade gracefully (queue-throttling before 503).
- Add synthetic warmup traffic test when scaling up region replicas during failover to ensure cache warmup completes before routing full traffic.
- Improve visibility on client retry loops (expose retry_count in logs).

Notes to self: keep this doc as informal breadcrumbs. When we move to the postmortem, copy the timeline and command snippets verbatim to the confluence postmortem. Also attach the heap dumps and kube event extracts.

Raw command outputs saved to: /tmp/incident-2026-03-03/taylor/ (kube-logs.txt, proxy-logs.txt, prometheus-query-results.json)

End of notes.
